audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings do not reflect the latest debt burden
audit_findings.magnitude: approximately $10.1 million annual pre-tax effective interest on the new $3.5 billion notes, computed from filed effective rates; 2.6% of the $383.3 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The FY2025 OE anchor retains interest expense but excludes the effective-interest cost of the May 2026 notes, while their proceeds enter the latest cash bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, we had $ 4,140.0 million in aggregate principal amount of convertible senior notes outstanding that are senior unsecured obligations with fixed annual interest rates.
audit_findings.explanation: The timing mismatch is demonstrated. However, both new tranches have zero cash coupons and filed effective rates of only 0.231% and 0.348%. Their approximately $10.1 million annual pre-tax cost is small relative to the anchor and far below the $69.75 per-share gap between the $105.22 price and $35.47 bull value, so it cannot change the present valuation conclusion by itself.
audit_findings.action: Pro forma FY2025 OE for the approximately $10.1 million annual pre-tax effective-interest run rate, apply the supportable tax effect, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Convertible dilution and retained interest describe different claims
audit_findings.magnitude: 112.638 million gross note-conversion and warrant shares; total denominator exceeds the August 3, 2026 outstanding shares by 122.208 million, or 85.0%
audit_findings.mechanism: Gross conversion and warrant capacity is included in fully diluted shares while OE retains note interest and principal remains a cash-settled debt claim; note hedges are not coherently reflected.
audit_findings.evidence: At their option, holders may exercise the conversion right of the respective Notes at the following specified times and rates to receive the principal amount in cash and receive any amount in excess of the principal amount in cash, shares of the Company’s common stock or a combination of cash and shares of the Company’s common stock, at the Company’s election.
audit_findings.explanation: The inconsistency is demonstrated by the filed terms and the 265.925 million-share denominator. The notes and warrants each cover 56.319 million shares, although principal must be settled in cash, note hedges offset conversion dilution, and warrant strikes range from $155.02 to $282.68 versus the $105.22 valuation price. This denominator treatment is large enough to materially depress every per-share value.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild the denominator tranche by tranche using one settlement state at a time, incorporating principal cash settlement, applicable interest treatment, note-hedge offsets, and only in-the-money incremental warrant shares; then rerun value per share and buy-below levels.

audit_findings.title: Uncommenced co-location leases are absent from the anchor run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $278.0 million undiscounted commitment over one to twenty years; annual OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Lease expense beginning after FY2025 can reduce future OE if projected revenue and growth do not recover the added co-location cost.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had additional operating leases for co-location arrangements that had not yet commenced of $ 278.0 million, of which a majority will commence in 2026, with lease terms of one year to twenty years .
audit_findings.explanation: The absence from FY2025 expense is demonstrated, and a majority of the leases were expected to commence in 2026. Filed first-half 2026 co-location cost increased $27.414 million, or 16%, year over year, but the record does not isolate how much came from these leases or the associated incremental revenue. The total commitment cannot be treated as an annual expense, so materiality remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the commenced-lease schedule, annual fixed and variable rent, June 2026 expense attributable to these sites, utilization, and related revenue; pro forma the OE anchor for the net run-rate contribution and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Repeated restructuring costs may have been misclassified
audit_findings.magnitude: $58.051 million in 2025, equal to 15.1% of the $383.3 million anchor; $95.441 million in 2024 and $56.643 million in 2023
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding recurring severance and reorganization costs back overstates normalized OE, while retaining genuinely nonrecurring impairments understates it.
audit_findings.evidence: Over the past several years, we have implemented internal restructurings and reorganizations designed to reduce the size and cost of our operations, improve operational efficiencies and reprioritize investments, enhance our ability to pursue market opportunities and accelerate our technology development initiatives.
audit_findings.explanation: A classification error is not yet demonstrated because the OE reconciliation was not supplied. Nevertheless, charges occurred in three consecutive years and the 2025 amount is material relative to the anchor. The filing identifies both workforce costs and asset impairments, so blanket inclusion or exclusion could materially change normalized OE.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile every annual OE adjustment to the restructuring roll-forward; retain recurring severance, reorganization and contract-termination costs, separately assess the $22.2 million acquired-intangible and $9.4 million internal-software or facility impairments, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Growth may depend on acquisitions whose cash cost is outside owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: filed acquisition cash outlays of $85.042 million in 2025, $566.901 million in 2024 and $227.156 million in 2023
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquisition-supported revenue enters historical and projected growth while acquisition cash outlays may be excluded from OE and acquired-intangible amortization may be added back.
audit_findings.evidence: We expect to continue to pursue acquisitions and other types of strategic relationships that involve technology sharing or close cooperation with other companies.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash outlays are large relative to the $383.3 million anchor, but the record does not establish that the 3% or 5% growth cases require acquisitions. The filing says acquired businesses were not material to consolidated results while acknowledging acquired customer contracts benefited delivery revenue. Dependence and the sustainable acquisition allowance therefore remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Prepare organic revenue and OE growth by solution, trace acquired-customer revenue and margins, identify acquisition-related amortization added back to OE, and rerun any growth case that requires acquisitions with a recurring acquisition-cash allowance.

audit_findings.title: Deferred-compensation assets may have been added without the matching claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $29.0 million obligation, approximately $0.11 per valuation share and 0.33% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted mutual funds associated with deferred compensation can enter cash and short-term investments while the matching participant liability is omitted from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025 and 2024, the total cash obligation under the deferred compensation plan was $ 29.0 million and $ 26.6 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 investment balance includes $32.078 million of mutual funds, and the latest separately disclosed plan obligation is $29.0 million. If the bridge includes the assets without the claim, value is overstated, but a full $29.0 million adjustment is only about $0.11 per share and cannot materially affect the $33.11 base value or the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the restricted mutual funds into the $3.355 billion cash-and-STI bridge and, if included, deduct the corresponding June 2026 deferred-compensation liability.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2016 $78.6 million, FY2022 $102.7 million and FY2024 $105.5 million residual D&A; FY2025 eligible amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Eligible non-economic depreciation or amortization left as an expense reduces historical OE and potentially the FY2025 anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2016 $78.6m (23.5% of filed D&A); FY2022 $102.7m (17.3% of filed D&A); FY2024 $105.5m (16.3% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: The treatment is demonstrably conservative rather than value-inflating. The historical residuals are sizable, including $105.5 million in 2024, but no evidence identifies an eligible portion or quantifies the FY2025 residual applicable to the anchor. The possible understatement may affect value, but its materiality cannot be established from the current record.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile FY2025 filed D&A by asset class and operating function, identify only components meeting the owner-earnings add-back policy, and rerun the valuation if filed evidence supports an additional add-back.
